title: Wan2.2-S2V-14B model card
claims: Audio-driven model: reference image plus audio file plus optional text prompt, optional pose video.
Output length follows the audio length unless num_clip is set.
Supports 480P and 720P; the output keeps the reference image aspect ratio.
Single-GPU run needs at least 80 GB VRAM.

title: InfiniteTalk: Audio-driven Video Generation for Sparse-Frame Video Dubbing
claims: Argues that mouth-only dubbing leaves face expression and body gestures out of sync with the new audio.
Sparse-frame dubbing keeps a few reference keyframes (identity, gestures, camera path) and regenerates the rest in sync with audio.
Streaming generator, arbitrary length, uses context frames for smooth chunk transitions.
notes: Authors own claims; no independent check.

title: Taming Multimodal Joint Training for High-Quality Video-to-Audio Synthesis (MMAudio)
claims: Generates audio from video with an optional text prompt.
Joint training on text-audio data and video data raises semantic fit and quality.
A frame-level synchronization module aligns video features with audio.
157M parameters; about 1.23 s to make 8 s of audio, per the authors.

title: HunyuanVideo-Foley: Multimodal Diffusion with Representation Alignment for High-Fidelity Foley Audio Generation
claims: Text-and-video-to-audio model for sound effects matching on-screen events.
Trained on about 100k hours of automatically annotated multimodal data.
Fuses video and audio with joint attention and injects text through cross-attention to balance the two inputs.

title: ThinkSound: Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs for Audio Generation and Editing
claims: Three stages: base foley from the video, object-centric refinement, then editing by natural-language instruction.
Introduces AudioCoT, a dataset linking visuals, text and sound with reasoning notes.
Reports strong results on the out-of-distribution Movie Gen Audio benchmark.

title: Veo (Google DeepMind model page)
claims: Veo 3 generates sound effects, ambient noise and dialogue natively with the video.
Scene extension tries to keep audio consistent with the original clip.
Admits natural, consistent speech, especially short segments, is still an area of active development.

title: Google's generative video model Veo 3 has a subtitles problem
claims: Veo 3 often burns gibberish subtitles into frames, likely because its training videos carry subtitles.
Google Labs staff said subtitles can be triggered by speech and a fix was in progress.
An outside researcher says negative prompts like "no subtitles" are usually less effective than positive instructions.
User workarounds: regenerate, remove text in post, crop the frame.

title: Kling 2.6 Review and Prompt Guide for Perfect Native Audio Sync
claims: Structure: scene, subject, motion and camera, then audio, with dialogue in its own block.
Tag speakers ([Character A]) and add a tone note; two-speaker exchanges are most reliable, three or more blend voices.
With many voice instructions speech can drift after about 5 to 6 s; native speech is English and Chinese, others are translated.
Use 10 s for dialogue, 5 s for ambient or SFX clips; 10 s max; draft with audio off because audio doubles credit cost.
Voice Control in image-to-video binds a voice to a character as [Character@VoiceName].

title: How to keep an AI voice consistent across every video clip
claims: Lock one voice source or voice ID per character and never swap tools mid-series.
Record stability, pace and tags in a one-line note per character.
Generate all of one character's lines in one session on the same settings so drift shows at once.
Use audio tags such as [whispers] for one beat instead of loosening stability for a whole scene.

title: Google Veo 3.1 (hands-on notes)
claims: Voices and background sound do not carry over between generations, even with a fixed seed.
Stitched segments each get a different voice; background sounds may stop.
Video extension on an earlier Veo version gave silent talking, because the extension model had no audio.
One creator matched voices with an ElevenLabs voice changer.

title: Seedance complete guide: audio and video generation
claims: Put dialogue in its own block naming speaker, language and tone; each line can use its own language.
Keep each speaker turn under 12 words; clips run 4 to 12 s.
Keep the whole prompt near 100 to 150 words; overlong prompts let audio drift from the picture.
Sound effects bind to on-screen events at frame level, so describe the action that makes the sound; you can state "no music".
Lists English, Mandarin, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Indonesian plus regional Chinese dialects.
notes: A search summary of another site said voice is limited to Chinese and English: the sources disagree.

title: LTX-2: Efficient Joint Audio-Visual Foundation Model
claims: Open model generating video and audio together, in sync.
Asymmetric dual-stream transformer: 14B video stream, 5B audio stream, bidirectional cross-attention.
Makes speech, background sound and foley fitting the scene; weights and code are public.

title: OmniHuman-1: Rethinking the Scaling-Up of One-Stage Conditioned Human Animation Models
claims: Animates a single image from audio, video or both; handles portrait to full body.
Supports speech and singing and human-object interaction.
Mixing several motion conditions in training is how the authors enlarge usable data.

title: LatentSync: Taming Audio-Conditioned Latent Diffusion Models for Lip Sync
claims: Audio-conditioned diffusion lip sync is weak because models take a shortcut and ignore the audio-lip link.
SyncNet supervision plus a more stable SyncNet raised its accuracy on HDTF from 91% to 94%.
TREPA aligns temporal representations to keep frames consistent.

title: ACE-Step: A Step Towards Music Generation Foundation Model
claims: Open diffusion music model: up to 4 minutes in about 20 s on an A100.
Supports lyric editing, remixing, voice cloning and track generation per the authors.
About 15 times faster than LLM-based music baselines.

title: FFmpeg filters documentation (acrossfade, loudnorm, sidechaincompress, adelay)
claims: acrossfade overlaps two streams by a set duration (default 44100 samples), with selectable curves.
loudnorm defaults: integrated -24, LRA 7, true peak -2; two-pass use needs measured_I, LRA, TP, thresh.
sidechaincompress defaults: threshold 0.125, ratio 2, attack 20 ms, release 250 ms; used to duck music under speech.
adelay delays channels by milliseconds by default.
notes: Read in slices; only the named filters were read.

title: Voice changer (ElevenLabs docs)
claims: Converts source audio into a chosen cloned voice while keeping whispers, laughs, accents and emotion.
Maximum segment 5 minutes; multilingual v2 covers 29 languages.
Set remove_background_noise to reduce room sound in the output.
Can build consistent character voices across languages and recording sessions.

title: Text to speech (ElevenLabs docs)
claims: Output is not deterministic; the seed helps but small differences remain.
Models cover 29 to 90+ languages; pick a voice whose accent matches the target language.
Previous/next text parameters keep prosody natural across chunks.
PCM tops out at 44.1 kHz; only Opus offers 48 kHz.

title: Timed Text Style Guide: General Requirements
claims: Minimum 5/6 of a second per subtitle event (20 frames at 24 fps), maximum 7 seconds.
At most two lines per subtitle; break after punctuation or before conjunctions and prepositions.
Keep articles with nouns and names together on a line.
notes: Reading speed and line length live in a separate Netflix article that was not opened.

title: Runway API models guide
claims: Lists ElevenLabs speech models, speech-to-speech, dubbing, voice isolation and sound effects as separate audio models.
Marks Veo 3.1, Wan 3.0, Grok Imagine and MiniMax H3 Max as native-audio video models; Kling 3.0 and Seedance 2.0 as optional audio.
Characters model makes a speaking character video from a script or audio file.

title: Text to speech best practices (ElevenLabs docs)
claims: Audio tags go in square brackets, e.g. [whispers], and some may be spoken as sound effects, so test.
Break tags are not supported in v3 and v4; use ellipses and punctuation for pacing.
Phone numbers, dates and units can be mispronounced; expand them in the text first.
Speed range is 0.7 to 1.2; extremes may hurt quality.

title: WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format
claims: Timestamps use a full stop before three millisecond digits; hours are optional.
Cue settings (position, line, size, align) follow the timing line.

title: SubRip (SRT) file format
claims: Block = index, timing line, text, blank line.
Timing is HH:MM:SS,mmm with a comma before milliseconds.
No official encoding; YouTube accepts only UTF-8.

title: Sound effects (ElevenLabs docs)
claims: Effects run 0.1 to 30 s; loop mode gives seamless ambient beds.
Describe action, setting and atmosphere ("rain against a window in a quiet apartment") not a category.
Exact repetition counts are not always followed.
Non-looping WAV output is 48 kHz.

title: Improving lip sync quality (sync.so docs)
claims: Wants near-frontal faces, even light, and a clear mouth; occlusions and profiles cause artifacts on older models.
Feed clean single-speaker speech without music or crowd noise.
Processes in about 30 to 40 s chunks, with quality dips at chunk joins; split long videos.
For teeth and beards use the pro tier; keep the face at least 480p.

title: How AI lip sync works (sync.so docs)
claims: Changes only the lip and lower-face region; background, body and hair stay as they were.
Generates mouth shapes in 2 s chunks, imitating the speaker's own mouth style.
Meant for dubbing and localization from one recording.

title: Sora 2 is OpenAI's consistently inconsistent AI video creator
claims: Finds Sora 2 audio often flat, muffled or metallic and unevenly balanced.
Sora makes ambience, effects and dialogue in one pass and cannot separate the layers.
Recommends adding ambience, effects and music in post.

title: Sora 2 Audio Engineering Guide
claims: State the sound hierarchy in the prompt (dialogue over ambience) with rough level offsets.
Keep spoken phrases short and use explicit speech verbs; test on a short low-resolution clip first.
Japanese speech sounded robotic in the author's tests; a silent video plus separate TTS was suggested.
For fine control extract audio, adjust levels and remux.

title: ACE-Step v1 3.5B model card
claims: Apache 2.0 licence.
Outputs vary a lot with seed and duration; repaint and extend can give unnatural joins.
Tracks beyond 5 minutes may lose structure; vocals are coarse; quality varies by language.

title: HunyuanVideo-Foley model card
claims: Input is a video plus an audio description text; batch mode reads a CSV.
Outputs 48 kHz audio.
Licence is tencent-hunyuan-community, not a standard open licence.

title: MMAudio model card
claims: Checkpoints are CC BY-NC 4.0: non-commercial use only.

title: InfiniteTalk model card
claims: Works as video dubbing (video plus audio) or image plus audio to video.
Claims unlimited duration; no technical limit given.
Apache 2.0; users are responsible for unlawful or misleading uses.

title: AI Music Licensing Explained (2026)
claims: Suno free tier is non-commercial; paid tiers grant commercial rights to downloaded output.
Udio paid plans grant commercial use; export to streaming is getting stricter.
A platform licence does not guarantee copyright; human authorship strengthens a claim.
Sony was still litigating against both; terms change without notice.

title: Stable Audio 2.5 announcement
claims: Tracks up to three minutes with intro, development and outro structure.
Audio inpainting continues a track from an uploaded clip.
Trained on a fully licensed dataset and called commercially safe by the vendor.

title: How to solve Veo 3 keeps generating unwanted dialogue
claims: A visible face, microphone or camera-facing pose pushes Veo toward speech.
Phrases like "no talking" can plant the idea of speech.
Fixes: describe a closed mouth and a concrete ambient soundscape, say the character is alone, give any voice to a narrator, keep prompts simple.
Open mouths in reference images can trigger speech.

title: Why your clip adds random dialogue or music and how to control it
claims: If a prompt never mentions sound, the model fills in plausible music, distant voices or extra lines.
Words like "interview", "crowd", "epic" or "montage" imply speech or a score.
Extend and bridge steps act like new generations, so the soundtrack can change at the seam.
Fix: a separate hearing block with MUST NOT lines (no voices, no music) restated in every extend prompt.

title: Kling AI Lip Sync Tutorial: Steps, Limits & Languages
claims: Video up to 60 s; longer footage must be split and rejoined.
Front-facing faces work best; distortion beyond roughly 30 degrees of turn.
TTS script must fit the clip length or it is cut or misaligned; supports CN, EN, JP, KR, ES.
Text artifacts seen in TTS output; switching to uploaded audio is the suggested workaround.

title: The ultimate prompting guide for Veo 3.1
claims: Writes spoken lines in quotation marks with a speaker tag ("A woman says, ...").
Labels sound effects "SFX:" and background sound "Ambient noise:".
Audio works in image-to-video, ingredients and first/last-frame modes; object add/remove edits give no audio.
notes: Quotes here, no quotes in the Google example: disagreement.

title: Sora 2 vs Veo 3.1: 7 audio prompts
claims: Reported that Sora 2 added subtle music despite instructions and mistimed a siren.
notes: Only the headline and a syndicated snippet seen; page truncated.

title: EU AI Act Article 50: transparency obligations
claims: Providers must mark synthetic audio and video as machine-readable where feasible.
Deployers of audio deepfakes must disclose them; evidently artistic or fictional work gets a lighter duty.
Article 50 applies from 2 August 2026 (commentary; check the text).
notes: Fetch failed; claims come from search results of several compliance blogs.

title: Can I create a Professional Voice Clone of someone else's voice?
claims: A professional voice clone can only be made of your own voice, after verification.
The voice owner may share a verified clone with you through a private link.
notes: Fetch returned 403; claims from search result text.

title: Wan 2.5 complete guide
claims: Wan 2.5 makes voice, ambience and lip sync in one pass and can take an uploaded voice track.
Audio language follows the prompt language; Chinese prompts reported most reliable.
Clips up to 10 s at 24 fps in most sources.

title: Veo 3 native audio prompt guide 2026
claims: Says "no music" is the one negative worth including because unrequested soundtrack is the most common failure.
